summary: FOUND BY THE CP-069 GREP, NOT BY THE SCANNER. After fixing the two known unflagged sinks in Wave 34, discover ran the grep that CP-069 requires — `rg -n "new URL\('/api/" app lib` — and found a THIRD instance of the identical defect class, structurally the same as the news sink that was just fixed. lib/opportunities/rss-opportunities-service.ts:38 builds `new URL('/api/feed/rss-news', params.origin)` and calls the global `fetch()` on it once per each of six hardcoded categories. `params.origin` is `request.nextUrl.origin` at BOTH callers: app/api/opportunities/sync/route.ts:13 and app/api/opportunities/route.ts:36. A caller who controls the `Host` / `X-Forwarded-Host` header therefore chose the destination of six concurrent server-side requests, and because the global `fetch` follows redirects, a 3xx from the first hop reached anywhere. CodeQL has never flagged it: js/request-forgery treats request.url as a remote-flow source but not request.nextUrl.origin. discover CANNOT fix it — lib/opportunities/** is outside the Wave 34 file ownership — and did not try. The fix is the same import swap that fixed the news sink two hours earlier: the frozen route key `newsRssFeed` already exists in lib/discover/internal-json-fetch.ts, so `ingestOpportunitiesFromRss` needs no new route map entry at all.
working_set: lib/discover/internal-json-fetch.ts (NEWS_UPSTREAM_ROUTES.newsRssFeed — the destination key that already exists)
completed: Confirmed the full taint path by reading the three files rather than inferring it: request.nextUrl.origin (reflects the inbound Host / X-Forwarded-Host header) at app/api/opportunities/sync/route.ts:13 and app/api/opportunities/route.ts:36 -> ingestOpportunitiesFromRss({ origin }) -> new URL('/api/feed/rss-news', params.origin) at lib/opportunities/rss-opportunities-service.ts:38 -> fetch(endpoint.toString(), { cache: 'no-store' }) at :40, inside a six-way categories.map fan-out.

Established that no validation or allowlist exists anywhere on that path, and that the transport has none of the five transport-level controls: no redirect denial, no resolve-then-pin, no timeout, no response cap, no content-type requirement.

Established that this needs no new infrastructure: the frozen route key `newsRssFeed` -> `/api/feed/rss-news` with params `limit` and `category` already exists in INTERNAL_UPSTREAM_ROUTES, and the `category` values this call site sends are already in the declared param set. The fix is replacing the three lines with a `fetchInternalJson({ route: 'newsRssFeed', params: { limit, category }, allowlist })` call.

Ran the same grep across app/ and lib/ and triaged every remaining `request.nextUrl.origin` hit so the next lane does not have to re-derive them. Classified as NOT the same defect, deliberately not reported as vulnerabilities: lib/auth/request-public-origin.ts is already env-first and hard-refuses the header in production, and its output feeds redirects rather than a network sink; app/api/music/share-message/route.ts:18 and app/api/payment/route.ts:120 are env-first with a request-origin fallback and build user-facing links, not server-side fetch destinations. app/api/admin/tours/[id]/collaboration-invites/route.ts:37 and the app/api/marketplace/integrations/shopify/* files are other lanes' and were read only far enough to classify.
Recorded the finding in DISC-002's blockers and in the discover domain state so it cannot be lost at handoff.
CONSUMED IN WAVE 35. Resolved; no further routing needed.
